criteria.commensurate: No. Seed 25 notice is 0.09 s at base and 0.79 s at end (+0.7 s of the seed's +15.0%); seed 39 notice at 20 hh is 0.11 s and 0.93 s; seed 39 notice at 10 hh is 0.08 s and 0.50 s. That buys nothing on the board: the same entrance placement, now 9 ft (seed 25) and 14 ft (seed 39 at 20 hh) off the tread instead of 4 ft. The layout stages that carry the gained fidelity stay flat (homesteads seed 25 1.21 s and 1.08 s; windbreak 0.47 s and 0.45 s). The web growth on seeds 4 and 39 at 20 hh (+0.8 to +0.9 s) is layout variance, not paid-for work: seed 47 at 20 hh web fell 1.47 s to 0.61 s in the same pair.
criteria.necessary: Partly. The values that trigger the growth are what feature 328 asks for: the 80 ft belt is MIN_BELT_DEPTH_FT from research 0071, and the privy and woodshed edges are measured past the wall gap. The board's widen step is the existing labels-L4 rule for a placement with no verge seat. The seconds themselves are not necessary: they come from how the unchanged search widens, not from work the new values require.
criteria.no_way_around: There is a way around. The widened entrance pass samples the full 60 ft band of every main and web route (seed 25: 17 routes, 3,764 seats, 7,932 houses._fits calls, each scanning static hard ground, bund walls and field chains). Only afterwards does it keep the seats within KOSATSUBA_ANCHOR_BAND_FT of the anchor and passing entrance_seat_ok. The anchor is known before sampling, so routes and candidates can be pruned by anchor distance before _fits, or _fits can be indexed. The session's explanation names the second itself. That is the per-candidate scan of unchanging geometry that dev/performance.md describes.
